justification: B is directly supported: where villagers cut a new pole each summer, the proportions ‘tycks ha närmat sig formen i den närmaste by som hade en sparad stomme att gå efter.’ A reverses that statement, since the text says ‘närmat sig’ rather than moved away. C applies the stability claim to the opposite case—‘Där stommen ... togs in och sparades ... rörde sig måtten knappt’—whereas without a saved frame ‘gled proportionerna.’ D is unrelated to the change described: the association merely ‘har bett att få ta hand om stommen,’ and Bjärnmo refused that request.

D matches both parts of the passage: ‘Stommen för bara skelettet vidare,’ while in Rossmåla ‘lövningen lades om två gånger under samma period.’ A is contradicted by Bjärnmo’s words, ‘Vi har aldrig bestämt hur den ska se ut. Den ligger ju där.’ B is a near-miss because the frame is ‘en instruktion’ and removes the need to remember, but it does not prescribe renewed decoration: ‘Det som måste göras om från början varje år kan lika gärna göras annorlunda.’ C adds an origin claim the text does not make; the stated observation is only ‘en skillnad mellan byar, inte mellan år,’ followed by evidence about stability and convergence.
